analysis: Reviewed three modified files. (1) ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift lines 299-305: after preload completion, enqueueSelectedModelRecovery is called for skipped, memory-failed and not-attempted candidates, guarded by Task.isCancelled, isShuttingDown and startupPreloadStopRequested. The recovery implementation (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery) is not in the supplied evidence. It must keep allowEviction:false, honor servingDrain/shutdown, and use only the advertised set, with no retirement bypass. A model retired after a failed self-test must not be re-loaded through this path. The retirement guards (failedSelfTestHashes, isRefusedByRetirement) are not shown applied to the recovery. This is an unverified contract, not a finding. It does not touch the A-001, A-003 or TB-002 data paths directly. (2) ProviderLoop+StartupShutdown.swift lines 60-107: shutdown unload is now bounded at 15s per slot. Slots whose unload does not finish are abandoned and left resident until process exit, which is logged. Security effect: shutdown cannot hang forever (availability gain; T-043 and T-029 relate). Residual risk: decrypted prompt and KV data in unified memory (T-028, T-014) persists until the process exits, but process exit releases it. The code runs after coordinatorClient.shutdown, inflight drain and App Attest worker stop, so authorization and connection state are already torn down. The write-behind SSD cache donation pipeline (T-041) could be cut off mid-flush if the process exits while an unload is abandoned. Write uses atomic tmp+rename and DBK3 AES-GCM, so partial artifacts are not expected to be readable. Per-slot cache flush ordering is not shown. The ShutdownUnloadFlag class is lock-protected and the detached sleep is fine. A latent logic quirk: when another task owns the unload, the loop waits for slot removal or the deadline, which is acceptable. (3) ProviderLoop+Testing.swift: test-only seams for selected-model recovery, with no production exposure and no #if DEBUG gating. The pre-existing seams are the same style. Remaining questions for integration: the SelectedModelRecovery source (admission, drain, retirement checks, memory floors) and the unloadModel cache-flush behavior on abandonment.
